Load your ROM to play

These change your running game's save data straight away, so they're for testing. Save normally in the game if you want to keep a change.

Pack your replacement files (textures, models, sounds) into a mod the game loads. Give each file the same path as the original it replaces; use the folder box for a prefix such as alt. A mod installed here stays on this device and loads at every start.

        
        

        

      
Makes a patch from your edited ROM. Pick the original, unmodified ROM first, so the patch applies only to the base game (and cannot be applied on top of another hack). The ROM never leaves your device.

      How the map is stored (a short guide)
      

        
A summary of Understanding Zelda 1 Screens, Columns, and Tiles. It explains what you are looking at in the tabs below, and what to change if you hack the game.

        
The building blocks

        
    
          
  • Tile: the basic picture on the NES, 8 by 8 pixels.
    • 
          
  • Block: four tiles in a 2 by 2 square, 16 by 16 pixels (like the question-mark block in Super Mario Bros.).
    • 
          
  • Column: 11 blocks stacked top to bottom.
    • 
          
  • Screen: 16 columns side by side. The overworld is 128 screens, but only 121 different layouts are stored, so 7 screens are shared.
    • 
        

        
Blocks (overworld)

        
    
          
  • Blocks 00 to 0F are free-form: each one lists its own four tiles. Block 05 is plain water, for example. The first four are used by dungeon passage and item screens, and block 04 is unused.
    • 
          
  • Blocks 10 to 37 are stored as a single number. The game takes that tile and the next three in the tile sheet, so a block like that needs four tiles that sit next to each other.
    • 
          
  • Special blocks 26 to 2B are the ones you interact with: pushable rock, bombable wall, burnable tree, pushable tomb and the two armos. Their real picture comes from a short replacement table.
    • 
        

        
Columns and how they are squeezed

        
A column is stored as bytes, and each byte carries three things: bit 7 means a column starts here, bit 6 means draw this block twice, and the other six bits are the block number (00 to 3F). So DB 4E 4E 4E 0E 1A 1B is only 7 bytes, yet it expands to the full 11 blocks: two rocks, seven ground blocks and two rocks. A column can also start in the middle of another one, so columns overlap and share bytes. Three columns that look almost the same can fit in 9 bytes instead of 33.

        
The 16 column groups each hold up to 16 columns (the game ships with 9 or 10 in each). A column's name is two digits: the first is the group, the second is its place in that group. For example C1 is the waterfall column, the second one in group C.

        
Screens

        
A screen is just 16 column names, one per column, with no compression. A table of 128 numbers then says which stored layout each spot on the world map uses. The start screen, for example, begins 01, A7, 84, 90, 10, 02, A5 and so on.

        
Dungeons

        
Dungeons work the same way with fewer parts. There are only 8 floor blocks (a block, floor, two monster statues, stairs, sand, water, black). Dungeon columns have 1 to 7 bytes and a repeat count of up to 7, rooms are 12 bytes each, and there are 10 column groups. Walls and doors are added separately, so a room's layout does not include them.

        
Where it lives in the ROM (file positions, with the 16-byte header)

        
    
          
  • Overworld screens: starts at $15428, 16 bytes each
    • 
          
  • Which layout each map square uses: $18590 (128 bytes, lowest 7 bits)
    • 
          
  • Pointers to the 16 column groups: $19D1F (the groups themselves start at about $15BE8)
    • 
          
  • Dungeon rooms: $160EE, 12 bytes each; their column group pointers are at $16714
    • 
        

        
Tools

        
Zelda Map Generator is a graphical viewer for these tables, and this tab does the same job for the overworld. There is no graphical tool that can edit columns yet, so edits are made on the bytes directly.

Pokémon Box

        
Drag Pokémon between the party and the PC boxes, in one game or across Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold/Silver/Crystal, Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald and FireRed/LeafGreen. Gen 1 ↔ Gen 2 follows the Time Capsule's rules; Gen 3 games trade with each other as a link cable would; Gen 1 and 2 Pokémon can be brought forward to Gen 3 (as Nintendo's later Poké Transporter did: same species, level, moves, names and shininess; nature from experience points; held items stay behind). The Items view next to each save's Pokémon lets you add, remove and reorder bag and PC items. It works on your last in-game save.

Pokémon

        
Load a Pokémon ROM once (with Remember it on this device ticked) and the game's own pictures appear on the Pokédex. For Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed and LeafGreen, the 3D map and where each Pokémon lives are read from your ROM too.

        
Pokémon Box (in the Pokémon tab) moves Pokémon between your saves by dragging them:

        
  • Red/Blue/Yellow ↔ Gold/Silver/Crystal, with the Time Capsule's rules
  • Between Gen 3 games, like a link-cable trade
  • Gen 1 and 2 Pokémon brought forward to Gen 3 (they keep their species, level, moves, names and shininess; held items have to come off first)

        
Above each save's Pokémon, Items switches to its bag and PC items (add, remove, change amounts, reorder) in every Pokémon game. For Red/Blue/Yellow and Gold/Silver/Crystal, Edit changes money, badges, your Pokémon's levels and moves, and the Pokédex.

        
Save in the game before you start, press Save changes when you're done, and Undo if you change your mind.

      

    

    

      
Ace Combat 3

        
This plays the Japanese version, which has the full story, with the English fan translation built in. You need your own discs as .bin files: Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere (Japan) Rev 1, disc 1 and disc 2.

        
The first start takes a minute while it builds the English discs; after that it's quick. If something's wrong, Your discs shows which version you loaded.

        
The checklist is a tree of the story's mission paths. It sits under the Ace Combat 3 mission briefing in the Strangereal Map, which is the Ace Combat tab.

      

    

    

      
Golden Sun

        
Golden Sun and The Lost Age each have their own page in the Golden Sun tab, with every Djinni (28 and 72), the summon tablets and the Psynergy items, and where to find them.

        
While you play Golden Sun here, the Djinn and Psynergy items your party collects tick themselves off. The Lost Age is ticked by hand for now.

      

    

    

      
Emulators

        
The Emulators tab is a general retro player, separate from the checklists. It plays Genesis / Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear, NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance games (.md .gen .sms .gg .nes .sfc .gb .gbc .gba, or a .zip of one).

        
It keeps a library of the games you add, four save-state slots per game, and a save-state editor with value search. Controls can be rebound, and controllers and touch buttons work. Everything stays in this browser.

      

    

  

  

    

      
Welcome to Triforce

      
Keep track of everything you collect in classic Zelda, Pokémon, Golden Sun and Ace Combat games, see where things are on a 3D map, and play the games right here in your browser using your own copies.

      
No installsBring your own gamesNothing is uploadedWorks with controllers

    


    
How it works

    
    
      
  1. Pick a game. Use the tabs at the top. Each game has a checklist of everything worth collecting, and most have a map.
    2. 
      
  2. Tick things off. Tap a tile to tick it. Hover over it (or tap and hold) to see where it is and how to get it.
    3. 
      
  3. Or let your save do it. Import save file reads a save from an emulator (.sav or .srm) and ticks everything you've already done. It only adds ticks, never removes them.
    4. 
      
  4. Play in your browser. Play in browser, then Choose ROM file to load your copy of the game. Each time you save in the game, the checklist fills itself in.
    5. 
    


    
Guide

    

      
Playing games

        
Load the file for your own copy of the game:

        
  • NES: .nes · Super Nintendo: .sfc .smc · Game Boy / Color: .gb .gbc
  • Game Boy Advance: .gba · Nintendo 64 (Ocarina of Time): .z64 .n64 .v64
  • PlayStation (Ace Combat 3): the disc images, .bin

        
Tick Remember it on this device and the game is there next time with Play saved ROM. The keys for each game are listed under the screen. Plug in a controller and it just works; Controls and Controller let you change the buttons. Full screen makes the game as big as your screen.

        
Your in-game saves are kept here too. Export save downloads one, Use a save file loads one you already have, and on some games Edit save opens a save editor.

      

      
The maps

        
Most games have a 3D model of the world under the checklist. Drag to turn it, scroll (or pinch) to zoom, and right-drag or Shift-drag to move.

        
Whole map shows everything, Top-down looks straight down, Orbit slowly circles, and Free roam lets you fly around. Tap a place's label to show only the things found there; the numbers show how many you have.

      

      
Your data

        
Everything stays on your computer, in this browser. Your games and saves are never uploaded, and no game files come with Triforce.

        
Your checklist progress is also kept with your account, so it follows you to your other devices.

        
Back up my progress, at the bottom of a game's page, saves your progress and saves to a file. Restore a backup brings them back, or moves them to another computer or browser.

        
Reset this game's progress clears one game's checklist.

      

    

    
About and credits
    
Triforce is one HTML file, written in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework, and built with Claude. Everything else it does stands on these projects:

    

      
Playing the games
    
        
  • JSNES — NES
    • 
        
  • GameBoy-Online — Game Boy and Game Boy Color
    • 
        
  • LakeSnes — Super Nintendo, compiled to WebAssembly
    • 
        
  • IodineGBA with the Cult-of-GBA BIOS — Game Boy Advance
    • 
        
  • Ship of Harkinian — Ocarina of Time, compiled to WebAssembly
    • 
        
  • Gen1Recomp — Pokémon Red, Blue and Yellow, run through love.js
    • 
        
  • Ace Combat 3 static recompilation — rebuilt for the browser, with Team NEMO's English patch
    • 
      

      
Emulators tab
    
        
  • libretro cores compiled to WebAssembly: Genesis Plus GX (Genesis, Master System, Game Gear), FCEUmm (NES), Snes9x 2010 (SNES) and mGBA (Game Boy family)
    • 
      

      
Maps, lore and tools
    
        
  • three.js — the 3D maps and the Strangereal Map
    • 
        
  • Golden Sun Password Generator, from Dyrati's password research
    • 
      

      
Saving and sharing
    
        
  • IndexedDB and localStorage — progress, saves and ROMs stay in your browser
    • 
        
  • Cloud sync when Triforce is opened as a Claude artifact
    • 
        
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages — the code and the public site
    • 
      

      
Building and modding
    
        
  • Emscripten and Binaryen — turning C and C++ into WebAssembly
    • 
        
  • RetroLab — the project's own Node.js toolkit for studying and modding games (in the repository)
    • 
        
  • Geist and Geist Mono — the type
    •
